title: 2165-sparse-identification-nonlinear-dynamics-conformal-prediction
universal_lens: The primitive unifies sparse dynamical system identification with distribution-free conformal prediction. By mapping the SINDy coefficient regression to a non-conformity scoring problem, it guarantees marginal coverage of future state transitions and discovered governing equations under exchangeability, bypassing restrictive Gaussian noise assumptions inherent in classical Bayesian inference.
gsi_mapping: GSI maps this operator to its calibration lane by replacing naive Bayesian posterior intervals with EnbPI. Cross-season out-of-bag residuals form the non-conformity distribution, yielding honest, distribution-free uncertainty bounds for both point forecasts and the structural stability of discovered feature terms across shifting NFL regimes.
gse_mapping: GSE utilizes these primitives to enforce calibrated situational reasoning. The conformal PID controller dynamically adjusts interval quantiles based on real-time miscoverage errors, ensuring that every published state-transition equation maintains strict long-run coverage guarantees even when facing non-Gaussian process noise or sudden tactical regime shifts.

reasoning_traces.think:
The core mathematical derivation rests on decoupling the discovery of sparse nonlinear dynamics (SINDy) from the probabilistic calibration of its outputs. Classical SINDy solves an L0-regularized least squares problem to find coefficients \Xi minimizing \|\dot{X} - \Theta(X)\Xi\|_2^2. However, the resulting coefficients lack rigorous uncertainty bounds under non-Gaussian noise. Fasel (2025) introduces Ensemble-SINDy (E-SINDy), generating B bootstrap resamples to create an ensemble of models. To guarantee coverage, they map the residuals of out-of-bag samples to non-conformity scores s_t^{(b)} = |y_t - \hat{f}_b(x_t)|. By taking the (1-\alpha)-quantile of these scores, they construct prediction intervals C_\alpha that satisfy P(Y \in C_\alpha) \ge 1-\alpha purely under exchangeability. Furthermore, they extend conformal prediction to the coefficients themselves using a jackknife+ approach (Feature-CP), measuring the L1 deviation of coefficients when specific library features are omitted. A dual duality emerges: while EnbPI handles forward-time prediction uncertainty, the Conformal PID controller acts as a feedback loop, adjusting the quantile threshold q_t in real-time based on cumulative miscoverage errors. This creates a self-calibrating dynamical system where the uncertainty bounds actively correct themselves against empirical violations, a crucial property for handling the regime shifts inherent in complex systems like sports analytics.

It bridges the gap between symbolic regression and modern statistical learning theory, evolving from simple bootstrap aggregations (EnbPI) into adaptive, closed-loop control mechanisms for uncertainty quantification. reasoning_traces.theory_of_mind: From a decision-theoretic perspective, the modeler acts as an agent seeking to publish robust governing laws. The conformal PID controller represents an opposing actor—the environment—continuously testing the validity of these laws. If the modeler's intervals are overconfident, the environment generates miscoverage errors, forcing the controller to widen the bounds. This adversarial calibration ensures that the published equations remain epistemically honest regardless of hidden noise structures.
reasoning_traces.cross_layer_veto: A strict veto condition applies to the LOCO feature importance operator: if the correlation matrix of the candidate library features exhibits near-singular eigenvalues, the leave-one-covariate-out scores will be severely biased downward due to compensating covariates. In such highly collinear regimes, the structural stability metrics become unreliable, and the primitive must fallback to standard ensemble inclusion probabilities to prevent discarding valid physical terms.
